Google Health setup

Google Health is an optional beta feature. It keeps a read-only copy of your Google Health data (exercise, sleep, activity, measurements, and heart rate) on your own server, and imports exercise routes as tracks. Errors and sync interruptions may occur. To use it, see the Health guide. This page covers setup.

Before you start:

  • You need your own Google Cloud project with access to the Google Health API. Google decides who gets access, and its rules can change. Check Google's requirements first.
  • Your Google Account must be linked to an active Google Health profile. If needed, create one or move your Fitbit account in the Google Health mobile app; see Google's account requirements.
  • In Google's Testing mode, you must reconnect every seven days. Your stored data stays.
  • One Google account per MTL Explorer installation.

Health data and route locations are sensitive. Protect the database, backups, login, and reverse proxy. Health data is stored in the database, and routes in ./data/gpx/google-health/. Back up ./data/postgis and ./data/gpx together.

Without Google credentials, the feature simply stays unconfigured. To turn it off completely, set MTL_GOOGLE_HEALTH_ENABLED=false in .env.

Each installation connects to Google directly, so your health data never passes through a third-party service. That is why every installation needs its own Google setup.

One-time installation setup

In MTL Explorer, open Settings → Import & sync → Google Health → Start setup. The setup assistant shows the scopes, an .env template, server checks, and links to each Google page: Cloud Console, API Library, Auth Platform, Audience, OAuth Clients, and Data Access.

  1. Select a Google Cloud project and enable Google Health API.

  2. Open Google Auth Platform. If Google shows Get started, fill in:

    • App name: enter MTL Explorer.
    • User support email: select your email, then select Next.
    • Audience: select External unless all users belong to the same Google Workspace organization, then select Next.
    • Contact Information: enter your email, then select Next.
    • Finish: accept the user-data policy, then select Continue and Create.

  3. Open Audience. Check that the publishing status is Testing and the user type is External. Under Test users, select + Add users, enter the Google account that owns the health data, and select Save. Check that the account appears in the list.

    Google will warn that the app is unverified. This is expected. Keep the app in Testing: this is the supported setup. You don't need to publish the app or have it verified by Google. The only drawback is reconnecting once a week.

  4. Open Clients and create an OAuth client:

    • Application type: select Desktop app.
    • Name: enter MTL Explorer.
    • Select Create, then Download JSON and save the file.
    • Before closing Google's dialog, copy the Client ID and Client secret. You need both in step 6.

  5. Open Data Access, select Add or remove scopes, and add the four read-only scopes:

    https://www.googleapis.com/auth/googlehealth.activity_and_fitness.readonly
https://www.googleapis.com/auth/googlehealth.health_metrics_and_measurements.readonly
https://www.googleapis.com/auth/googlehealth.sleep.readonly
https://www.googleapis.com/auth/googlehealth.location.readonly

    Tip: Select Copy all four scopes in the assistant, paste them into Manually add scopes, then select Add to table, Update, and Save. The first three are required. Location is optional and only needed for exercise routes.

  6. Add the client ID and secret to .env, next to docker-compose.yml. Create .env first if it is missing:

    MTL_GOOGLE_HEALTH_CLIENT_ID=your-client-id.apps.googleusercontent.com
MTL_GOOGLE_HEALTH_CLIENT_SECRET=your-client-secret

    Keep this secret. If you change it later, you must reconnect Google Health. Your stored health data stays.

  7. Apply the change:

    docker compose up -d

    Do not use docker compose restart; it does not load the new settings. Wait until MTL Explorer is back, sign in, return to the assistant, and select Check again.

If you keep .env elsewhere, use docker compose --env-file "/path/to/mtl.env" up -d. On a NAS, add both settings to the stack environment and recreate the app container.

Advanced: if MTL Explorer runs behind HTTPS and you prefer an automatic callback, set MTL_GOOGLE_HEALTH_REDIRECT_URI to its public HTTPS callback address and use a Web application OAuth client with exactly the same address. Leave it unset for the normal setup.

See Google Health authorization for why the setup works this way.

Connect the Google account

  1. Open Settings → Import & sync → Google Health.
  2. In the setup assistant, select Open Google consent.
  3. On Google's Select what this app can access screen, select Select all and Continue. You can leave Location unchecked if you don't need exercise routes.
  4. Google opens http://127.0.0.1:1/mtl-explorer-oauth and the browser shows an error. This is expected. Copy the complete address from the address bar.
  5. Return to MTL Explorer, paste the address, and select Complete connection within ten minutes.
  6. Select Open Health, or open Manage to review access. Follow the sync link to Processing to watch the first import.

The last 24 hours appear first; the rest of the week and older history follow over time. Temporary errors are retried automatically. Settings → Processing shows what failed and when it is retried next.

Reconnect

When access is about to expire or has expired, Settings shows a message. Select Reauthorize, open Google consent, copy the new address, and paste it into MTL Explorer. Your Google setup and stored data stay unchanged.

Diagnose Google Health

To see recent Google Health activity in the server log:

docker compose logs --since 30m app | grep 'Google Health'

The log never contains tokens, health data, or locations. When reporting a problem, include the complete error and stack trace around the failing job.

To stop syncing, select Disconnect Google; your data stays. To delete the local copy, disconnect first, then select Delete local mirror and type DELETE. This removes only Google Health records and routes.

Synchronization settings

Most installations don't need to change these. Add them under mtl.google-health in the server configuration.

Setting Default Meaning
history-start-date 2010-01-01 Oldest day to import
recent-window P7D Days that are checked again for late changes
recent-fast-window PT24H Range checked on every sync
recent-full-interval PT24H How often the whole recent window is checked
sync-interval PT30M Time between syncs
cycle-deadline-margin PT1M Time kept free before the next sync
history-budget-fraction 0.5 Share of sync time used for older history
history-stream-quantum PT1M Time needed to start another page of history
database-transaction-timeout PT5M Time limit for saving one batch
work-failure-limit 4 Attempts before a failing range is skipped
work-retry-max-delay PT6H Longest wait between retries
max-chunk-rows / max-chunk-bytes 100000 / 67108864 Size limit per batch

See synchronization for how syncing works and which values are allowed.
